slides.main: Blaming your last meal? Symptoms can start hours later.
slides.sub: How to keep a food diary that actually shows patterns.

slides.main: Food intolerance symptoms usually start a few hours after eating and can last days.
slides.sub: On a bad day, look back over the previous 24 to 48 hours.

slides.main: Write down how much, not just what you ate.
slides.sub: A splash of milk in your coffee and a large milkshake are not the same.

slides.main: Log stress and sleep, the columns most people skip.
slides.sub: Otherwise bread can look guilty when a stressful week made the difference.

slides.main: Treat what you find as a lead to check, not a diagnosis.
slides.sub: Do not cut foods out without advice from a doctor or dietitian.

slides.main: See a doctor if symptoms keep coming back, or if you have:
items: Blood in your stool or black stools
Symptoms that wake you up at night
